newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index plunges 4.06 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index plunges 4.06 pct at close.

text.p: The Philippine stock market's main index ended 109.46 points lower, or 4.06 percent, at 2,589.20 points on Wednesday, the biggest drop in three months, on uncertainties over the peso, brokers said.
"It's very bad as foreign funds are out of the Philippines and the region because of concerns about the peso," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.

"People do not know what the Central Bank is up to, whether they will continue to defend the peso or not. It's driving the people out of the equities market," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities.
Investors panicked after the Singapore Straits Times newspaper reported that the Monetary Board will discuss the devaluation of the peso in its meeting today.
Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista who was quoted in the Straits Times report denied the report.
The foreign exchange market was however still nervous and the Central Bank resorted to heavy dollar selling in early trade to defend the peso.
The stock market reacted to the renewed concerns on the currency by across-the-board selling.
PLDT closed 25 pesos lower at 890 pesos, Metrobank down 20 pesos at 505 and Meralco B down nine pesos at 127 pesos.
In the broader market, losers trounced gainers 141 to 10. All sectors fell. Turnover was moderate at 2.2 billion pesos.
The composite index pierced two support levels at 2,650 points in midsession and 2,600 towards close.
The main index posted its second biggest day drop for the year, the first in April when it shed 128.87 points, or 4.54 percent to 2,708.44.
"There should be some upside on Wednesday after three days of successive losses of over 160 points," said Carl Valentin, trader at Asia Pacific Capital Equities.
But some were not as optimistic.

"I do not discount the possibility that we may even test a support of 2,300. The speculation on the peso has brought about this bearish scenario," said Jonathan Ravelas, chief technical analyst and head of sales at Asian Capital Equities.
